issues.description: Method naming mismatch for the order-serving routine in SealSaloon: the problem statement (UML and textual description) requires a public method named checkOrderReady() that is called by orderMeal() to attempt serving queued orders. In the solution implementation the same behavior is implemented in a method named processOrders(), and orderMeal() calls processOrders() instead. This naming inconsistency between the specified API (checkOrderReady) and the provided implementation (processOrders) can confuse students about which method name/signature they must implement to match the specification and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API names consistent. Either (A) rename the solution's processOrders() method to checkOrderReady() and update calls so orderMeal() invokes checkOrderReady(), or (B) add a public checkOrderReady() method that delegates to the existing processOrders() (i.e., public void checkOrderReady() { processOrders(); }) so the class exposes the method name required by the UML/problem statement and tests. Alternatively, if the specification should use processOrders(), update the problem statement/UML to reference processOrders() instead.
